what: Audit of the F.15 curator-agreement ladder: is the standardisation pipeline confounded with the equivalence relation, and is each rung the harness's own criterion?
source_pairs: GLORYx 37 drugs co-curated by this corpus; same construction as scripts/annotation_agreement.py

census.note: No salt/multi-fragment structure occurs on either side, so FragmentParent is inert here; the corpus records no stereocentre anywhere, so every stereo-rung gain is a configuration-unspecified vs configuration-specified match, never an enantiomer conflation.

hygiene_held_fixed_factorial.design: Cleanup+FragmentParent+Uncharge applied to BOTH sides at every cell, vs applied at none; crossed with tautomer-canonicalisation on/off and stereo kept/dropped; InChIKey representation.
hygiene_held_fixed_factorial.reading: Salt-stripping and neutralisation change nothing at any rung, so they are effectively held fixed across all five criteria. The ladder's spread is stereo (~0.24), not hygiene (0.000); tautomer contributes ~0.01-0.02 on THIS set.

criterion_consistency_defect.finding: Four of five rungs are identical between scripts/annotation_agreement.py and the paper's harness (grail_metabolism.metrics._match_keys). CANONICAL is not: the F.15 script uses Chem.MolToSmiles(mol) (stereo-AWARE) while the harness's _canonical_key uses isomericSmiles=False (stereo-BLIND), and every method table in the paper uses the harness.
criterion_consistency_defect.monotonicity: Under the harness criterion the five rungs are NOT nested: canonical (0.2413) sits ABOVE full InChIKey (0.1452), so 'strictest to most tolerant' mis-describes the order.

regenerate: scripts/annotation_agreement.py, replacing its local key_of() with grail_metabolism.metrics._match_keys so the rung definitions match every other table.
